judged_text: createEvent now matches destinationCalendar by credentialId and falls back to calendarId 'primary' when no destination matches, whereas the previous code wrote to the destination row's own externalId. Legacy destinationCalendar rows with a null credentialId (the case the old no-credentialId branch in createAllCalendarEvents existed for) get every booking event written to the credential owner's primary calendar instead of the selected one, and the no-credentialId branch — which calls createEvent once per matching credential — writes one event per credential, all onto primary, silently misfiling booking data.

adjudication.rationale: In GoogleCalendarService.createEvent the target calendar is now chosen by `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, with fallback `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`. In EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents, the `else` branch for `destination.credentialId` missing still calls `createEvent(c, event)` for each matching credential (now passing `credential.id` into calendar.createEvent), but because the destinationCalendar entries have no matching `credentialId`, `find(...)` returns undefined and every insert falls back to "primary". Previously, GoogleCalendarService used `destinationCalendar.externalId` directly, so the no-credentialId branch would still write to the selected externalId, not primary. This means legacy destinationCalendar rows without credentialId can be silently mis-filed onto primary (and multiplied across credentials).
